html:
The Mau Mau uprising was a rebellion in central Kenya, mainly among the Kikuyu, against British rule and settler land seizure, during which a state of emergency lasted from October 1952 to 1960.

Fighters of the Land and Freedom Army took oaths and fought from the forests of Mount Kenya and the Aberdares. They killed fewer than 40 white civilians but many more Africans seen as loyal to the government. Britain jailed Jomo Kenyatta, sent troops and bombers, and held tens of thousands in camps, where torture was common, as at Hola. The fighter Dedan Kimathi was captured and hanged in 1957.

Over ten thousand rebels were killed. The rising convinced Britain that settler rule could not last, and Kenya became independent in 1963. In 2013 Britain paid compensation to thousands of survivors of the camps.
sum: The Mau Mau uprising was a rebellion in central Kenya, mainly among the Kikuyu, against British rule and settler land seizure, during which a state of emergency lasted from October 1952 to 1960.
